title: NASA CEA — LOX / LH2 performance, O/F 6.0, 1000 psia, Ae/At 40

source.documents: NASA RP-1311 Part I (1994) and Part II (1996)
source.retrieved_from: RocketCEA v1.2.3 documentation, which reproduces the program's own printed output verbatim
source.independence: Produced by the 2002 Fortran implementation of CEA. The provider under test is the v3 re-implementation (cea 3.3.4), so neither number in the oracle comparison produced the other.

reference_condition_note: CEA's printed Cf and Isp columns are the optimum-expansion values: the momentum term alone, with the exit pressure matched by the ambient. Measured on the v3 provider across all three chemistry modes, Cf_printed + (pe/pc)*Ae/At equals Ivac/c* to between 6e-09 and 4e-07, which is what establishes it. A vacuum figure compared against these would be high by the whole pressure term — 5.6 % on this class of case.

case.chamber_pressure_note: 1000.0 psia, converted with the exact definitions of the pound-force and the inch
case.temperature_note: The source prints 90.18 K for O2(L) against the 90.17 K used here. Immaterial, and the reason is itself a Phase 5C finding: CEA models O2(L) with an assigned enthalpy, so neither value enters the calculation.

published.label: Characteristic velocity  c*
published.conversion_note: The international foot is exactly 0.3048 m.

published.label: Specific impulse  Isp
published.conversion_note: CEA v3 returns an effective exhaust velocity in m/s; seconds follow from the standard gravity 9.80665 m/s². RocketForge never labels a value in m/s as an Isp.

validates.reason: The published values were produced by a shifting-equilibrium, calorically imperfect calculation. RocketForge v1 is a constant-property, calorically perfect model. Agreement or disagreement between them is a model difference, and calling the residual a RocketForge error would be reporting a deliberate modelling choice as a defect. The oracle is validated against this source; RocketForge is then compared against the oracle, under its own stated assumptions.

verification.note: Direction is always published value -> compare -> computed value. Nothing in RocketForge reads these numbers to produce a result.
